land.text: the Kashmir valley: the infobox lists the Alchon Huns and the Gonanda dynasty (II) as predecessors

predecessors.note: The alchon-huns dossier ends the Kashmir line of the Alchons in c. 630; the Karkota page has Durlabhavardhana found the dynasty in 625.

land.text: all of the Karkota kingdom: 'his son Avantivarman deposed Utpalapida and claimed the throne c. 855'

capitals.name: Srinagara (Srinagar)
capitals.note: The page calls Srinagara the other capital, which 'continued to serve' beside Parihasapura; Pravarapura, built by Pravarasena, is the old city. The Karkota page's infobox names only Parihaspur.

capitals.name: Parihasapura (Parihaspur)
capitals.note: 'A new capital at Parihasapura', founded by Lalitaditya (reign 724-760); the page gives no founding year, so 724 is the start of his reign. The coordinate is approximate (Parihaspora, Baramulla).

rulers.name: Lalitaditya Muktapida
rulers.note: c. 724/5-c. 760 (Sen); Kalhana's 36 years 7 months 11 days is held incorrect.

rulers.name: Chippata-Jayapida
rulers.note: The table gives 832-885; the text has him crowned in 837/8 and murdered c. 840, and the Utpala page dates his death 'around 840'. The years after are puppet kings.

rulers.name: Puppet kings (Ajitapida, Anangapida, Utpalapida, Sukhavarma)
rulers.title: puppet rulers
rulers.note: Undated on the page ('~'); Avantivarman deposed Utpalapida c. 855.

correction.text: not a Karkota land before 625: Kashmir was the Gonanda II and Alchon line, drawn in alchon-huns until c. 630

keyframe_review.note: 127,000 km2 for 592-601 lies in Afghan Bactria, Badakhshan and Tajikistan (312 Bactria and 115 Badakhshan cells of 436), nowhere near Kashmir, and 33 years before the dynasty: the infobox gives 'Established: 625' and lists the Alchon Huns and the Gonanda dynasty (II) as predecessors. No area on the page. The Kashmir valley of these years is the Alchon (Gonanda II) line in alchon-huns.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 656 shape: the Kashmir valley, Poonch, Gilgit and the Punjab hills of the Karkota realm, without the Afghan half of the 626 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 625: Cliopatria's first usable shape begins in 626. Durlabhavardhana 'controlled vast swaths of territories including modern day Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa' (an assumption resting on Xuanzang's visit, May 631-April 633), which is the 656 shape; the Afghan half of Cliopatria's 626 shape is not there.

correction.text: the 626 shape without its Afghan half: Cliopatria's 656 shape, valid 626-655

keyframe_review.note: 209,000 km2 for 626-655, 439 cells of which (111,000 km2) are Afghan Tokharistan; the Durlabhavardhana page names only Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the Nezak page has Xuanzang find Taxila 'recently lost to Kashmir' c. 630. The Afghan part is removed; what is left is the 656 shape.

118,000 km2 for 656-731, no infobox area. Matches 'Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa' for Durlabhavardhana and Durlabhaka; the 'kashmir' row of Cliopatria (about 85,000 km2 in 656, no cell shared) is the other half of the same realm (notes).

119,000 km2 for 732-750: unchanged under Lalitaditya (724-760). The conquests of Kalhana (Kannauj, Magadha, Gauda, Kalinga, Gujarat, Tukharas, Tibet) are not drawn: Stein called the later ones 'manifestly legendary', Sen 'rejects the claimed Hindu Kush-Pamir conquests' and Huntington calls them 'massive raiding and looting expeditions rather than true conquests'.
123,000 km2 for 751-771: +4,000 km2 the page does not explain (Gilgit/Little Palur taken by the Tang in 747; Kashmir 'played a significant role' per Sen). Kept as drawn.
123,000 km2 for 772-849: no change; the pages give no border move under Jayapida (779-813) or his successors.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 850 unchanged, valid 850-855

keyframe_review.note: 123,000 km2 for 850-859 but the dynasty ends in 855: 'Avantivarman deposed Utpalapida and claimed the throne c. 855' (Utpala page), infobox 'Disestablished: 855'. Shape unchanged, valid 850-855; 856-859 belong to the Utpala dynasty.

region.text: Cliopatria's 656 shape: the Kashmir valley, Poonch, Gilgit and the Punjab hills of the Karkota realm, without the Afghan half of the 626 shape

ledger.note: 625: Durlabhavardhana founds the Karkota dynasty in Kashmir. Infobox 'Established: 625'; 'Durlabhavardhana: Founder, c. 625 (reign 625-662)'. Kalhana has him rise after Baladitya's death 'with help from a minister' (a tale Biswas rejects); he 'controlled vast swaths of territories including modern day Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa' (Durlabhavardhana page). The Nezak page has Taxila 'recently lost to Kashmir' at Xuanzang's visit c. 630. The page gives names, not a boundary.
724: Lalitaditya founds Parihasapura as a new capital. The page gives no founding year, so the start of his reign (c. 724/5) is used; Srinagara 'continued to serve'.

855: Avantivarman ends the Karkotas and founds the Utpala dynasty. 'His son Avantivarman deposed Utpalapida and claimed the throne c. 855 with help from minister Sura'; the Karkota infobox 'Disestablished: 855'. The last significant king, Cippatajayapida, died 'around 840'. Cliopatria runs the row to 859.

wars.name: Arab invasions of 713
wars.outcome: The Tang 'received an embassy from Candrapida requesting aid against Arab invasions' in 713; no help came, but 'Candrapida defended his territory'. No border moved.

wars.name: Lalitaditya's campaigns (Kalhana)
wars.outcome: Kalhana has Yashovarman of Kannauj submit after a long war (Jacobi 14 August 733; Stein before 736; Mishra after 736) and Jivitagupta of the Later Guptas beaten c. 735-736 (Goetz); the page records no land held, and Stein, Sen, Huntington and Davidson read them as legend or raids. Not drawn.
wars.note: The Magadha advance is placed in 733 and the return in 747 (Davidson). The Tang record has a Kashmiri envoy in March-April 733 calling Lalitaditya a vassal of the Heavenly Qaghan (Tang dossier).

wars.name: Tibetan invasion of Kashmir and the Tang capture of Little Palur
wars.outcome: Goetz dates a Tibetan invasion of Kashmir to c. 747; the Tang took Little Palur (the Gilgit valley) in 747 after three failed attempts with Kashmir's help (Sen); a Tokharistan envoy asked the Tang in 749-750 to renew its alliance with Kashmir. No border is stated.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier; the Pir Panjal and Karakoram limits of the kingdom are approximate throughout and the claimed conquests of Lalitaditya are not drawn.

notes: Five pages. Cliopatria's first three Karkota shapes (592-655, 127,000 and 209,000 km2) are mostly Afghan Bactria and Badakhshan, not Kashmir; they are marked wrong (592, 602) or adjusted to the 656 shape (626). The seed's neighbours list the Sasanians and Western Gokturks for them, which fits Tokharistan, not the Karkotas; a Tokharistan polity (Yabghus) has no dossier. The Cliopatria row 'Kashmir' (626-1343) shares not one cell with the Karkota shapes of 626-850 and adds about 85,000 km2 (656) to them: the two rows draw the two halves of the same realm; the 'kashmir' dossier (sa-03) and this one must be reconciled (merge the halves into one state or give the 'kashmir' half to this dossier for 626-855). The start (625) is five years before the alchon-huns dossier ends its Kashmir line (c. 630). Dates: Karkota infobox 625-855, Cliopatria 592-859. Chippata-Jayapida's reign is 832-885 in the table and c. 840 in the text. The Taxila gain is only a note (the 656 shape holds it). Lalitaditya's 733 Tang vassal letter is recorded by the Tang dossier. Gazetteer: all names found (Srinagar, Gilgit region); Parihasapura is not a place.
